headline: ATC (Agent Trust Card) built for AI agents to provide SSL-like trust and identity
summary: MarketNow introduces ATC, a solution akin to SSL certificates for AI agents, integrating identity, trust, encryption, translation, and payment to facilitate secure, autonomous agent commerce.
details: Just as websites rely on SSL certificates for trust, AI agents now have ATC (Agent Trust Card). This innovative solution combines identity, trust, encryption, translation, and payment capabilities into a single 'card' for AI entities.

ATC is a core component of MarketNow, an infrastructure designed to enable a future where AI agents can autonomously discover, verify, negotiate tasks, and transact with each other. It aims to build a foundation of trust in agent-to-agent commerce.

The full technical specification for ATC is available at marketnow.site/atc-spec.json, with comprehensive documentation at marketnow.site/atc. This project addresses the critical need for secure and verifiable interactions in the evolving AI agent ecosystem.
caption:
AI agents need trust and verifiable identity just like websites need SSL certificates. A new solution, ATC (Agent Trust Card), aims to provide exactly that.

headline_marked: [[GAUNTLEX tests AI code specs]] for security flaws before implementation
headline: GAUNTLEX tests AI code specs for security flaws before implementation
summary: This MIT-licensed engine runs a Builder and a Breaker agent simultaneously on a spec, generating adversarial tests before any code is written, addressing a critical gap in large-scale modernization projects.
details: GAUNTLEX is a new adversarial co-generation engine designed to test technical specifications for vulnerabilities before any code is written. It is free, MIT licensed, and works with various model providers, including fully local setups via Ollama.

Traditional security tools, like SAST and DAST scanners, typically attack code only after it has been implemented. This approach becomes unsustainable and ineffective at the scale of modern legacy modernization projects, where thousands of specifications are generated rapidly.

GAUNTLEX addresses this by treating specs and PRDs as separate inputs. It deploys two agents: a Builder, which implements the specification, and a Breaker, which simultaneously attacks the spec without visibility into the Builder's code.

By the time the Builder produces working code, the Breaker has already generated a comprehensive adversarial test suite. A third agent, the Arbiter, scores these attacks, and if the Adversarial Resilience Score falls below a set threshold (0.80 by default), the code merge is automatically blocked.

Findings are tied to real CWEs and mapped to compliance controls relevant for auditors, such as NIST SSDF, OWASP SAMM, SOC 2, and ISO 27001. Five regulated-industry playbooks (HIPAA, FINRA, PCI DSS, SOC 2, OWASP Top 10) are included, each mapped to specific regulations.

The engine is designed to integrate with existing workflows and model providers, offering flexibility for teams that cannot send code to external APIs. It aims to cover a critical security gap that current post-implementation testing methods miss.
